title: Opal Orchards on‑prem scaling and networking playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working draft playbook for Opal Orchards' on‑prem/private deployment. Audience: Opal infra lead (Maya Santos), Redwood field eng (Jordan, Priya), and platform eng who will author the Terraform modules and run the cutover. Goal: arrive at a deployable plan that meets Opal's latency and throughput targets while respecting their air‑gapped/limited‑egress constraints.

High‑level goals and acceptance criteria:
- Support Production footprint for: 10 sustained inference QPS (chat/generation mix), spikes to 120 QPS sustained for 10 min (harvest windows).
- Endpoint latency SLO: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for summary/generation small prompts (<=512 tokens). Embedding batch jobs allowed longer latency.
- Business requirement: all customer PII must remain on‑site, KMS integration with on‑prem HSM or Vault required.
- RPO/RTO: backups daily, RTO for control plane components < 4 hours (with documented manual recovery).

Scope and constraints (Opal specifics):
- Air‑gapped by default; limited outbound to designated Redwood relay at cutover windows only.
- Single primary datacenter in Portland site; optional DR in a secondary colocation (TBD).
- Power constraints: 40A rack circuits available initially — can host up to 4 high‑density GPU nodes per rack without additional power upgrades.
- Networking: existing on‑site fabric: 25GbE leaf/spine; ops team can provision 100GbE uplinks with 4‑week lead time.

Assumptions (please validate with Opal):
- Typical request size: 400 tokens input, 200 tokens output average (generation-heavy).
- Concurrent active sessions during peak: ~60 (chat sessions), with many short infrequent requests from telemetry agents.
- Batch/embeddings jobs run nightly with heavy I/O to local object store.
- Models to serve initially: 1x large LLM (~31B FP16), and a smaller reranker/embedding model.

Sizing recommendation (initial prod cluster - conservative):
- Inference nodes (GPU hosts): 4 nodes with 2 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (or equivalent H100 if available) per node. Rationale: each 80GB device can hold a 30B model with room for KV cache + headroom for batching.
  - Per node: 2x A100 80GB, 256 GiB RAM, 48 vCPU, 2 x 1.6TB NVMe (local), 1 x 10Gb management NIC + 1 x 100Gb (or 25Gb) data NIC.
  - Expected token throughput (approx): ~6–10 QPS/model per GPU for 31B generation under conservative batching config; cluster-level headroom for spikes achieved via short burst autoscaling (see autoscale notes).
- Control plane nodes: 3x m5‑class control VMs (or equivalent bare metal): 8 vCPU, 32 GiB RAM, 500GB disk; run Redwood private control plane, api-proxy, and metrics exporters.
- Model artifact storage: 1 x S3‑compatible object store (MinIO or Ceph RGW) + lifecycle to on‑node NVMe cache; provision 100TB usable object store for model versions, snapshots, and nightly embeddings.
- Autoscaling buffer: reserve 2x spare GPU nodes in rack for fast replacement and capacity buffer; if load demands increase plan +4 GPUs (2 nodes) to reach expected peak headroom.

Networking and top‑of‑rack design notes:
- Traffic separation: control plane and data plane separated via VLANs. API traffic from customer applications should hit API load balancer -> control plane -> ingress gateway -> inference nodes over private VLAN.
- Required ports: 443 (API), 2200 (SRE SSH bastion), 9090 (metrics), 50051 (gRPC model RPC) — limit to known IPs.
- Latency sensitivity: ensure <1ms leaf/spine hop latency; for KV cache access keep model serving traffic local to same rack where possible.
- Recommended switch config: enable jumbo frames for model shard transfers, BFD for fast failure detection, and MLAG/ECMP to balance load.
- Consider RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) if Opal plans multi‑node tensor parallel workloads in future. For initial deployment, use TCP over 25/100GbE.

Terraform module notes (implementation guidance):
- Module layout suggestions (names map to git modules):
  - modules/private/control-plane: resources for control plane services, systemd units, consul integration (if used).
  - modules/private/inference-host: hardware profile, device discovery, NVMe mount, cgroup and GPU driver install.
  - modules/private/object-store: MinIO deployment + bucket policies, kmswrap hooks.
  - modules/private/network: VLANs, firewall entries, LB objects (HAProxy/Envoy), SNAT/egress rules.
- State backend recommendation: Use a locked S3 backend. For air‑gapped: MinIO with consul/etcd for locking OR Terraform Cloud/Enterprise if Opal prefers hosted state. Document decision and runbook for state recovery.
- Variables to standardize across modules: region_name, rack_label, gpu_profile (A100_80GB | H100), local_nvme_mount, object_store_endpoint, kms_provider (vault|hsm).
- Outputs to expose: control_plane_lb, prometheus_endpoint, healthcheck_token, model_artifact_bucket.
- Module tests: include terraform validate, a small integration harness that provisions VM with docker and verifies GPU visibility (nvidia-smi) and ability to pull model tarball from MinIO.

Upgrade and rollforward plan (high level):
1) Preflight: build candidate AMI/OS image with GPU drivers, runtime, and quantization libs; smoke test on staging host.
2) Canary deploy: update control plane and edge gateway; route 2–5% traffic to canary inference nodes running new runtime/quantization. Monitor p50/p95 and token error rates for 24h.
3) Rolling upgrade of inference cluster: drain one node at a time, replace runtime artifact, warm KV cache using replay tool (see linked artifacts).
4) Full cutover: switch LB weights when all nodes pass smoke tests. Keep fallback policy: if p95 degrades >20% or error rate >0.5% for 30m automatically route to previous model variant/host.

Rollback steps (if cutover fails):
- Trigger LB weight reversal to previous control plane and inference instances (manual or automation).
- Redeploy last known good control-plane artifact to control nodes, reattach object store, and verify auth tokens.
- If object-store schema migration was applied, run migration rollback script (defined in github PR linked).

Operational runbook / cutover checklist (condensed):
- Pre‑cutover validation:
  - Confirm spare racks/nodes physically available and powered.
  - Verify firmware / BIOS GPU compatibility with selected drivers.
  - Confirm MinIO bucket replication and backup snapshot taken.
  - Validate Vault HSM connectivity and test key unwrap.
  - Smoke‑test model pull + local NVMe cache load.
- During cutover:
  - Pause non‑critical batch embedding jobs.
  - Start canary and watch telemetry: latency, token consumption, error rates, memory pressure, NVMe I/O.
  - Hold for 45–60 minutes at each traffic ramp step.
- Post‑cutover:
  - Run synthetic prompts covering top 50 user flows and verify outputs against golden set.
  - Collect evaluation metrics and store snapshot in Confluence.

Security and compliance notes:
- Integrate with HashiCorp Vault for secrets and optional HSM for KMS; record a key rotation cadence (every 90 days).
- Audit logging: ensure all inference requests and control commands are logged and exported to Splunk/ELK; mask PII fields at the api-proxy layer.
- Network ACLs: restrict Terraform state access to specific operator IPs and MFA protected bastion.

Monitoring and SLO measurement:
- Metrics to collect: per‑model request rate, token rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory utilization, NVMe I/O throughput, model cache hit ratio, queue length.
- Alerting thresholds (examples): queue_length > 50 (P1), GPU memory pressure > 92% for >5m (P1), p95 > target * 1.25 for 15m (P0).

Known unknowns / open questions (action items):
- Confirm exact rack power per candidate cabinets and whether additional PDUs needed (Opal ops).
- Confirm whether Opal can provision 100GbE uplinks within timeline (lead time 4 weeks).
- Clarify disaster recovery expectations and if warm DR cluster required.
- Which models will be allowed to auto‑update from model registry vs pinned per‑release?
- Does Opal require air‑gapped initial model upload flow (sneakernet handshake)?

Next steps and owners:
- Jordan: finalize hardware SKU list and cost estimate (due 2026‑03‑07).
- Priya: prototype terraform/integration test for inference-host module (due 2026‑03‑14).
- Maya (Opal): confirm rack power and network lead times (due 2026‑03‑02).
- Liam: draft vault/HSM integration design and installation runbook (due 2026‑03‑09).

Appendix: quick commands / snippets to be added into terraform module README later:
- Example variable snippet:
  variable "gpu_profile" {
    type = string
    default = "A100_80GB"
  }
- State recovery tip: to recover a lost terraform state in air‑gapped env, export MinIO bucket backup and use the terraform state replace‑providers and state push flow documented in linked PR.

End of draft.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally conservative for the first rollout. If Opal approves riskier options (e.g., single larger host with 8x GPUs or earlier 100GbE commitment) we can tighten cluster counts and reduce initial cost. Please flag any mismatches with Opal procurement or site constraints in replies below.
